messages:
eli: seeing a weird small-batch latency spike on canary after driver 553 deployed. median p99 up ~2.5x on 8-token seqs.
maria: saw the CI regression too, perf-bot posted a failure for nightly-tinybatch. link: https://ci/reports/1234 :grimacing: 
kai: suspect kernel selection flipped... KV cache hit rate dropped from 97% -> 62% on the same workload.
eli: profiling shows extra memcpy scheduling and a new coop-scheduler path in driver logs. snippet:
```
[triton_autotune] selected kernel matmul_f32_tile32x32
[driver] using cooperative_group_scheduler=true
cudaMemcpyAsync queued on stream 0x7f
```
nina: can you paste the perf record / nvprof? even a flamegraph would help.
eli: quick flamegraph from canary attached (truncated):
```
50% memcpy
20% matmul_kernel
15% kv_cache_lookup
10% sync_wait
```
maria: interesting - kernel changed to a tiling variant that causes non-coalesced loads for our KV layout.
kai: started a git bisect across rollout commits; suspect 2f9a3bd was the autoscheduler tweak that enabled cooperative scheduling for sm90.
ops: we can roll back the driver on canary, but that blocks rollout for a few hours. pref complex.
eli: repro steps for anyone: 
```
export RW_PREFETCH=1
python perf_runner.py --model tiny --seq 8 --batch 1 --iters 1000
```
eli: turning RW_PREFETCH=0 brings p99 back to baseline locally.
maria: temporary mitigation = disable coop-scheduler in runtime and pin kernel choice. can we push a canary patch?
kai: opening PR to add a runtime flag to force previous tiling kernel and disable coop scheduling via env var RW_COOP_SCHED=0
perf-bot: CI perf alert: nightly/torch2x-smallbatch latency +210% vs baseline
ops: agreed hold rollout until we validate patch in canary. assigning to @kai and @maria :thumbsup:
